shlokas.sanskrit: एष ते नृगशापस्य विस्तरो ऽभिहितो मया । यद्यस्ति श्रवणे श्रद्धा शृणुष्वेहापरां कथाम् ।। 7.55.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: eṣa te nṛgaśāpasya vistaro 'bhihito mayā | yadyasti śravaṇe śraddhā śṛṇuṣvehāparāṃ kathām || 7.55.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: This account of Nriga's curse has now been related to you by me in full; if you have the desire to listen, hear now this further tale.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण सौमित्रिः पुनरब्रवीत् । तृप्तिराश्चर्यभूतानां कथानां नास्ति मे नृप ।। 7.55.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evamuktastu rāmeṇa saumitriḥ punarabravīt | tṛptirāścaryabhūtānāṃ kathānāṃ nāsti me nṛpa || 7.55.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus addressed by Rama, Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra, spoke again: O king, there is no satiety for me of these wondrous stories.

shlokas.sanskrit: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राम इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । कथां परमधर्मिष्ठां व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.55.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: lakṣmaṇenaivamuktastu rāma ikṣvākunandanaḥ | kathāṃ paramadharmiṣṭhāṃ vyāhartumupacakrame || 7.55.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus addressed by Lakshmana, Rama, the delight of the Ikshvakus, began to relate a tale most full of righteousness.

shlokas.sanskrit: आसीद्राजा निमिर्नाम इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । पुत्रो द्वादशमो वीर्ये धर्मे च परिनिष्ठितः ।। 7.55.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: āsīdrājā nimirnāma ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām | putro dvādaśamo vīrye dharme ca pariniṣṭhitaḥ || 7.55.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: There was a king named Nimi, the twelfth son of the great-souled Ikshvaku, firmly established in both valor and righteousness.

shlokas.sanskrit: स राजा वीर्यसम्पन्नः पुरं देवपुरोपमम् । निवेशयामास तदा अभ्याशे गौतमस्य तु ।। 7.55.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa rājā vīryasampannaḥ puraṃ devapuropamam | niveśayāmāsa tadā abhyāśe gautamasya tu || 7.55.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: That king, endowed with valor, then founded a city resembling the city of the gods, in the vicinity of Gautama's hermitage.

shlokas.sanskrit: पुरस्य सुकृतं नाम वैजयन्तमिति श्रुतम् । निवेशं यत्र राजर्षिर्निमिश्चक्रे महायशाः ।। 7.55.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: purasya sukṛtaṃ nāma vaijayantamiti śrutam | niveśaṃ yatra rājarṣirnimiścakre mahāyaśāḥ || 7.55.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: The city which that royal sage Nimi of great fame established there as his settlement was well-built and renowned by the name Vaijayanta.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य सुमहापुरम् । यजेयं दीर्घसत्रेण पितुः प्रह्लादयन्मनः ।। 7.55.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā niveśya sumahāpuram | yajeyaṃ dīrghasatreṇa pituḥ prahlādayanmanaḥ || 7.55.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: After founding that very great city, a thought arose in him: 'I shall perform a sacrifice with a long sacrificial session, gladdening the heart of my father.'

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः पितरमामन्त्र्य इक्ष्वाकुं हि मनोः सुतम् । वसिष्ठं वरयामास पूर्वं ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमम् ।। 7.55.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ pitaramāmantrya ikṣvākuṃ hi manoḥ sutam | vasiṣṭhaṃ varayāmāsa pūrvaṃ brahmarṣisattamam || 7.55.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then, having taken leave of his father Ikshvaku, the son of Manu, he first chose Vasishtha, the most excellent of the Brahmin sages, as his priest.

shlokas.sanskrit: अनन्तरं स राजर्षिर्निमिरिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । अत्रिमङ्गिरसं चैव भृगुं चैव तपोधनम् ।। 7.55.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: anantaraṃ sa rājarṣirnimirikṣvākunandanaḥ | atrimaṅgirasaṃ caiva bhṛguṃ caiva tapodhanam || 7.55.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thereafter that royal sage Nimi, the delight of the Ikshvakus, chose also Atri, Angiras, and Bhrigu, rich in austerities.

shlokas.sanskrit: तमुवाच वसिष्ठस्तु निमिं राजर्षिसत्तमम् । वृतो ऽहं पूर्वमिन्द्रेण अन्तरं प्रतिपालय ।। 7.55.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tamuvāca vasiṣṭhastu nimiṃ rājarṣisattamam | vṛto 'haṃ pūrvamindreṇa antaraṃ pratipālaya || 7.55.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: But Vasishtha said to Nimi, that most excellent of royal sages: 'I have been chosen beforehand by Indra; wait for the interval until then.'

shlokas.sanskrit: अनन्तरं महाविप्रो गौतमः प्रत्यपूरयत् । वसिष्ठो ऽपि महातेजा इन्द्रयज्ञमथाकरोत् ।। 7.55.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: anantaraṃ mahāvipro gautamaḥ pratyapūrayat | vasiṣṭho 'pi mahātejā indrayajñamathākarot || 7.55.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thereupon the great Brahmin Gautama filled the office of priest in his stead, while Vasishtha of mighty splendor went and performed Indra's sacrifice.

shlokas.sanskrit: निमिस्तु राजा विप्रांस्तान्समानीय नराधिपः । अयजद्धिमवत्पार्श्वे स्वपुरस्य समीपतः । पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि राजा दीक्षामुपागमत् ।। 7.55.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nimistu rājā viprāṃstānsamānīya narādhipaḥ | ayajaddhimavatpārśve svapurasya samīpataḥ | pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi rājā dīkṣāmupāgamat || 7.55.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: But King Nimi, the lord of men, having assembled those Brahmins, performed his sacrifice on the slope of the Himalaya near his own city; and the king entered upon the consecration for five thousand years.

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रयज्ञावसाने तु वसिष्ठो भगवनृषिः । सकाशमागतो राज्ञो हौत्रं कर्तुमनिन्दितः ।। 7.55.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: indrayajñāvasāne tu vasiṣṭho bhagavanṛṣiḥ | sakāśamāgato rājño hautraṃ kartumaninditaḥ || 7.55.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: At the conclusion of Indra's sacrifice, the venerable and blameless sage Vasishtha came into the presence of the king to perform the office of the officiating priest.

shlokas.sanskrit: तदन्तरमथापश्यद्गौतमेनाभिपूरितम् । कोपेन महताविष्टो वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मणः सुतः ।। 7.55.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tadantaramathāpaśyadgautamenābhipūritam | kopena mahatāviṣṭo vasiṣṭho brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ || 7.55.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then Vasishtha, the son of Brahma, saw that the interval had been filled by Gautama, and he was seized with great wrath.

shlokas.sanskrit: स राज्ञो दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी मुहूर्तं समुपाविशत् । तस्मिन्नहनि राजर्षिर्निद्रया ऽपहृतो भृशम् ।। 7.55.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa rājño darśanākāṅkṣī muhūrtaṃ samupāviśat | tasminnahani rājarṣirnidrayā 'pahṛto bhṛśam || 7.55.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Desiring an audience with the king, he sat down for a while; but on that day the royal sage was deeply overcome by sleep.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो मन्युर्वसिष्ठस्य प्रादुरासीन्महात्मनः । अदर्शनेन राजर्षेर्व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.55.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato manyurvasiṣṭhasya prādurāsīnmahātmanaḥ | adarśanena rājarṣervyāhartumupacakrame || 7.55.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then anger arose in the great-souled Vasishtha, and on account of not being received by the royal sage he began to speak.

shlokas.sanskrit: यस्मात्त्वमन्यं वृतवान्मामवज्ञाय पार्थिव । चेतनेन विनाभूतो देहस्तव भविष्यति ।। 7.55.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: yasmāttvamanyaṃ vṛtavānmāmavajñāya pārthiva | cetanena vinābhūto dehastava bhaviṣyati || 7.55.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'Because you, O king, disregarding me, have chosen another, your body shall become bereft of consciousness.'

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः प्रबुद्धो राजर्षिः श्रुत्वा शापमुदाहृतम् । ब्रह्मयोनिमथोवाच संरम्भात् क्रोधमूर्च्छितः ।। 7.55.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ prabuddho rājarṣiḥ śrutvā śāpamudāhṛtam | brahmayonimathovāca saṃrambhāt krodhamūrcchitaḥ || 7.55.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the royal sage, awakened and hearing the curse that had been uttered, in his agitation, beside himself with anger, addressed him who was born of Brahma.

shlokas.sanskrit: अजानतः शयानस्य क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः । मुक्तवान्मयि शापाग्निं यमदण्डमिवापरम् ।। 7.55.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ajānataḥ śayānasya krodhena kaluṣīkṛtaḥ | muktavānmayi śāpāgniṃ yamadaṇḍamivāparam || 7.55.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: While I lay asleep, unaware, he, his mind clouded by anger, hurled at me the fire of a curse, like a second rod of Yama.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मात्तवापि ब्रह्मर्षे चेतनेन विना कृतः । देहः सुरुचिरप्रख्यो भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.55.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasmāttavāpi brahmarṣe cetanena vinā kṛtaḥ | dehaḥ suruciraprakhyo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.55.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Therefore, O Brahmarshi, your body too, though radiant and most beautiful in appearance, shall be deprived of consciousness; of this there is no doubt.

shlokas.sanskrit: इति रोषवशादुभौ तदानीमन्योन्यं शपितौ नृपद्विजेन्द्रौ । सहसैव बभूवतुर्विदेहौ तत्तुल्याधिगतप्रभाववन्तौ ।। 7.55.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: iti roṣavaśādubhau tadānīmanyonyaṃ śapitau nṛpadvijendrau | sahasaiva babhūvaturvidehau tattulyādhigataprabhāvavantau || 7.55.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus, overpowered by wrath, the two of them at that moment cursed one another—the king and the foremost of the twice-born—and both, possessed of equal power thus attained, were suddenly rendered bodiless.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 55 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe pañcapañcāśaḥ sargaḥ || 55 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the fifty-fifth canto in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the sacred Ramayana, the first poem composed by the sage Valmiki.
